result.summary: Several layout and overflow issues are visible: truncated restaurant names, clipped horizontal-scroll cards/chips, and a partially off-screen category control, which make the home feed look unfinished and harder to scan.

issues.description: In the “Fastest near you” row, the third restaurant title is cut off mid-word (“Trattoria Piccol”) with no ellipsis, so the name is unreadable.
issues.suggestion: Constrain card width consistently, apply single-line truncation with ellipsis (text-overflow: ellipsis), and/or allow the title to wrap to two lines so full names remain legible.

issues.description: The rightmost “Fastest near you” card (image and delivery-time pill) is heavily clipped by the screen edge, and the section does not clearly communicate a horizontal carousel.
issues.suggestion: Add peeking/padding on the trailing edge, consistent card gutters, and optional scroll indicators or snap points so cut-off content feels intentional rather than broken.

issues.description: Category filter chips overflow the viewport; a partial empty/white chip is visible on the far right with no clear affordance that the row scrolls.
issues.suggestion: Implement a proper horizontal scroller with end padding, fade edge, or chevron so users understand more filters exist, and avoid rendering a half-visible empty chip.

issues.description: The lower “Popular right now” pizza card is only partially visible (image and -20% badge) with no restaurant name or metadata yet in view, which can look like a broken/incomplete tile on first paint.
issues.suggestion: Ensure the first popular card fully fits above the tab bar on common viewport heights, or add slightly more bottom padding/safe-area spacing so key content isn’t obscured by the nav.

issues.description: Delivery-time badges sit over food imagery with light backgrounds; on bright plate photos (e.g. poke bowl) contrast and alignment look slightly uneven compared with darker burger/ramen cards.
issues.suggestion: Standardize badge contrast (stronger scrim or border), fixed positioning, and minimum contrast so labels stay readable on all thumbnail backgrounds.
